steps.name: environment
steps.description: Validate node/npm, ensure workspace exists, and persist HOST and PORT via /etc/profile.d simple script. Do not persist NODE_ENV globally. The profile.d script computes npm global bin at source time to avoid embedding writer PATH and prevents duplicate PATH entries. The atomic write is implemented with a temporary file created as the unprivileged user and moved into place with sudo, ensuring correct ownership and atomicity.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/simple-calculator-40856-40905/SimpleCalculatorApplication"
ERR_EXIT(){ echo "ERROR: $1" >&2; exit ${2:-1}; }
command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 || ERR_EXIT "node not found" 2
command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1 || ERR_EXIT "npm not found" 3
# Emit versions for diagnostics
printf "node: %s npm: %s\n" "$(node -v)" "$(npm -v)"
# Ensure workspace
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE"
# Create profile.d content in a tmp file owned by the current user, then install as root
TMPFILE="/tmp/simple_calculator_env.sh.$$.tmp"
cat > "$TMPFILE" <<'EOF'
# SimpleCalculatorApplication environment (generated)
# Export HOST and PORT for dev servers; do NOT set NODE_ENV globally here
export HOST=0.0.0.0
export PORT=3000
# At shell source time, compute npm global bin and append to PATH if present and not already included
if command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  NPM_GBIN=$(npm bin -g 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [ -n "$NPM_GBIN" ]; then
    case ":$PATH:" in
      *:"$NPM_GBIN":*) :;;
      *) export PATH="$PATH:$NPM_GBIN";;
    esac
  fi
fi
EOF
# Move into place atomically with correct permissions
sudo mv "$TMPFILE" "/etc/profile.d/simple_calculator_env.sh"
sudo chmod 644 "/etc/profile.d/simple_calculator_env.sh"
# Verify file
sudo -- sh -c 'test -f /etc/profile.d/simple_calculator_env.sh || exit 4'

steps.name: dependencies
steps.description: Install project dependencies in the workspace. Use deterministic heuristic: when package-lock.json exists compute its md5 and compare with cached .package-lock.md5 to decide whether to run npm ci. Ensure install runs if package.json was just created. Test devDependencies (@testing-library/*, jest) are only installed if TESTS=1 or FORCE_TEST_DEPS=1 to avoid unexpected lockfile changes; environment variable FORCE_INSTALL=1 forces reinstall.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/simple-calculator-40856-40905/SimpleCalculatorApplication"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
ERR_EXIT(){ echo "ERROR: $1" >&2; exit ${2:-1}; }
command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1 || ERR_EXIT "npm missing" 2
if [ ! -f package.json ]; then echo "no package.json found, nothing to install"; exit 0; fi
# Decide if install needed
DO_INSTALL=0
if [ ! -d node_modules ] || [ "${FORCE_INSTALL:-0}" = "1" ]; then DO_INSTALL=1; fi
if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then
  md5sum package-lock.json | awk '{print $1}' > .package-lock.md5.new
  if [ -f .package-lock.md5 ]; then
    if ! cmp -s .package-lock.md5 .package-lock.md5.new; then DO_INSTALL=1; fi
  else
    DO_INSTALL=1
  fi
  mv .package-lock.md5.new .package-lock.md5
fi
if [ "$DO_INSTALL" -eq 1 ]; then
  LOG=/tmp/npm_install_log.$$
  if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then
    npm ci --no-audit --no-fund >"$LOG" 2>&1 || { tail -n 200 "$LOG" >&2; ERR_EXIT "npm ci failed" 10; }
  else
    npm install --no-audit --no-fund >"$LOG" 2>&1 || { tail -n 200 "$LOG" >&2; ERR_EXIT "npm install failed" 11; }
  fi
else
  echo "node_modules present and package-lock unchanged; skipping install"
fi
# Install test/dev deps only if requested to avoid changing lockfile unintentionally
if [ "${TESTS:-0}" = "1" ] || [ "${FORCE_TEST_DEPS:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  npm i -D @testing-library/react @testing-library/jest-dom jest --no-audit --no-fund >/tmp/npm_test_deps_log.$$ 2>&1 || { tail -n 100 /tmp/npm_test_deps_log.$$ >&2; echo "warning: installing test deps failed" >&2; }
fi

steps.name: validation
steps.description: Validate the environment by serving the production build artifacts and verifying HTTP responses. Depends on environment, scaffold, dependencies and build. Prefer local node_modules/.bin/http-server if present; otherwise use python3 -m http.server. Poll only 127.0.0.1 and localhost and ensure robust process-group startup and cleanup.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/simple-calculator-40856-40905/SimpleCalculatorApplication"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
ERR_EXIT(){ echo "ERROR: $1" >&2; exit ${2:-1}; }
export HOST=0.0.0.0 PORT=${PORT:-3000} NODE_ENV=production
if [ ! -d build ]; then ERR_EXIT "build directory not found; run build step first" 40; fi
LOGFILE=$(mktemp /tmp/simple_calc_srvlog.XXXX)
# Choose server: prefer local http-server in node_modules, otherwise python fallback
if [ -x "./node_modules/.bin/http-server" ]; then
  setsid ./node_modules/.bin/http-server build -p "$PORT" -a 0.0.0.0 >"$LOGFILE" 2>&1 &
  PID=$!
elif command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v http-server >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  setsid npx http-server build -p "$PORT" -a 0.0.0.0 >"$LOGFILE" 2>&1 &
  PID=$!
else
  setsid python3 -m http.server "$PORT" --directory build >"$LOGFILE" 2>&1 &
  PID=$!
fi
trap 'pgid=$(ps -o pgid= $PID | tr -d " "); [ -n "$pgid" ] && kill -TERM -"$pgid" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; rm -f "$LOGFILE"' EXIT
# Wait up to 120s for HTTP response on 127.0.0.1 or localhost
MAX_WAIT=120
SLEEP=2
WAITED=0
while [ $WAITED -lt $MAX_WAIT ]; do
  if curl -sSf "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT" >/dev/null 2>&1 || curl -sSf "http://localhost:$PORT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "validation: server responded"
    break
  fi
  sleep $SLEEP
  WAITED=$((WAITED+SLEEP))
done
if [ $WAITED -ge $MAX_WAIT ]; then
  echo "validation failed: server did not respond within ${MAX_WAIT}s" >&2
  echo "---- last log lines ----" >&2
  tail -n 200 "$LOGFILE" >&2 || true
  ERR_EXIT "validation timeout" 41
fi
# Clean shutdown
pgid=$(ps -o pgid= $PID | tr -d " ")
if [ -n "$pgid" ]; then kill -TERM -"$pgid" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
wait "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true
rm -f "$LOGFILE"
echo "validation: success"

reasoning: Goal: produce a concise, idempotent, non-interactive setup plan that fixes the analyst's critical/high findings while preserving original steps. Key decisions: (1) Environment step now only persists HOST and PORT and adds an /etc/profile.d script that computes npm global bin at source time to avoid embedding writer PATH; TMP file ownership is handled so sed edits are executed with sudo to avoid permission issues and avoid persisting NODE_ENV globally. (2) Scaffold step removes all uses of Function/eval and replaces them with a small deterministic arithmetic evaluator (shunting-yard algorithm) implemented in pure JS so no runtime code generation is used; the evaluator does not depend on process.env.NODE_ENV. CRA invocation avoids non-standard --scripts-version flag and uses existing preinstalled create-react-app if present or npx create-react-app without --no-install to keep flow consistent; the relationship with the dependencies step is explicit. (3) Dependencies step uses deterministic heuristics: when package-lock.json exists, compute and cache its checksum in .package-lock.md5 and compare to decide whether to run npm ci; ensures install runs when package.json was just created by scaffold. It installs testing deps as devDependencies only when tests are requested (FORCE_TEST_DEPS=1) to avoid unexpectedly modifying lockfile, but will install them automatically if TESTS=1. (4) Test step is guarded: it will only create test files when jest and testing-library are present (installed) to avoid modifying repo state when tests cannot run; the script will exit with code 0 when tests are intentionally skipped to avoid ambiguous exit codes for orchestrators. (5) Build step category changed to 'build' and exports NODE_ENV=production for deterministic production builds. (6) Validation step serves the production build; it prefers node_modules/.bin/http-server if available, otherwise uses python3 -m http.server; it polls only 127.0.0.1 and localhost (not 0.0.0.0) and starts the server in its own process group and ensures robust cleanup. These changes implement the analyst recommendations at CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM levels while keeping scripts concise and idempotent. All steps use the authoritative workspace path and follow required bash structure and error handling.
